chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from some of his companions from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who performed the ritual bath for Ihram, then trimmed his nails, he said: 'He wipes them with water and does not repeat the bath.'

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And one does not enter Ihram in silk, nor in brocade mixed with the fur of rabbits or foxes, nor does one enter Ihram in black clothes, and the best clothes for Ihram are white ones made of cotton or linen.

key_terms.اِغْتَسَلَ لِلْإِحْرَامِ: performed the ritual bath for Ihram

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for clothing and grooming when entering Ihram in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that minor grooming acts like trimming nails after the initial Ihram bath do not break the state, requiring only a simple wipe rather than a full re-ghusl. It further establishes the jurisprudential preference for white cotton or linen garments while prohibiting silk and dark colors, reflecting the Sunnah of simplicity and purity in pilgrimage attire.
